framing_issues.text: No party disputes that ... (cards 1-9: lines 182, 194, 206, 218, 230, 242, 254, 266, 278; rule at line 167)
framing_issues.issue: Systematic universal negatives. Every card's 'What supports it' opens with 'No party disputes ...', and the 'Supported' label is defined that way. Yet the page says Resource Supply Management's testimony is unreadable, the Oct 15 hearing transcript has no file (P-003), and positions reportedly changed at that hearing (P-154, P-155). The page qualifies elsewhere ('Every plan we could read') but not here. Fix: 'No party whose testimony we could read disputes ...'.

framing_issues.text: That reading assumes base rates later absorb the full amount. (also line 116)
framing_issues.issue: Uneven, shaky caveat. It is attached only to GAM's distributional claim, twice, and is not quite right: GAM's ranking (classes whose fuel share exceeds their base share benefit more, relative to their bills) holds at any pass-through level. Only whether homes come out behind in net dollars depends on how much base rates absorb.

framing_issues.text: GIPL says new pipeline fees should be split like power-line costs (also Plan D line 144, card 4 line 216)
framing_issues.issue: Possibly outdated position stated as current. Georgia Power's rebuttal reports that GIPL's witness switched to an energy allocation at the hearing (P-154, P-155). Card 5's 'In short' and Plan D's 'What it does' still present the transmission-style split in the present tense. Card 4's 'In short' names only Georgia Power and GAM as opposing Staff's energy split and omits that GIPL may now be closer to Staff.

framing_issues.text: No party disputes that splitting by energy or by peak demand changes what each customer group pays.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context that flips the label. P-102 shows GIPL arguing against a Georgia Power position ('it does matter where these revenues are credited'; 'If the ratio of MWh to MW were the same for all classes, I would agree with Georgia Power'). Readers are not told Georgia Power apparently argued the opposite, and the card is labeled 'Supported' on this point.
